Academic scope: coworker feedback and research

Reviewed 4 November 2026. Several suggestions have a partial design, but the academic experience still needs complete grading-policy setup, student course grades, group work, and role-specific calendar workflows. This note records findings and proposed work. It does not approve or implement features.

Scope and evidence

The owner narrowed current work to students, professors and teaching assistants, then requested a comparison and research using the coworker's Whiteboard.pdf. Campus events, organizations, room booking, advising and institution-wide operations remain outside this review. The existing work is preserved.

Input: local Original coworker PDF (kept outside this package), two pages, 310,496 bytes, SHA-256 8674111c4651103a146b98da2856373d021006ef96a47c23aa3cad0b00fa618a. Both pages were text-extracted and visually inspected, including the activity-feed and Achievements screenshots. The PDF and screenshots were not uploaded or copied into the project. Public searches used generic feature questions.

The PDF has 17 numbered entries but 15 distinct topics: item 15 is the screenshot supporting item 14, and item 17 repeats and strengthens item 13. Preserve both references without counting duplicate features.

Coverage below means coverage in local concept sources, accepted designs, or planning records. No item is a production capability: Whiteboard still has no backend, production authentication, persistent records, live notifications or AI service. A control label, planning statement or navigation link alone does not establish a complete workflow. This review used source inspection, not a new browser usability test.

Research findings that affect the recommendations

Grading and group work come first

Blackboard documents points, weighted and custom overall-grade calculations, with item/category weights and calculation details for students. Whiteboard's opportunity is understandable configuration and trustworthy calculations; “Blackboard cannot weight grades” is not a supported competitive claim. [Overall Grade Column](https://help.anthology.com/blackboard/instructor/en/grading/grading-setup/grade-columns/overall-grade-column.html), [Course Grades](https://help.anthology.com/blackboard/student/en/grades/course-grades.html).

Proposed validation: configure Assignments 10%, Exam 1 25%, Exam 2 25% and Final 40%; map assessments; reconcile an independently calculated student example. Specify empty categories, missing versus ungraded versus excused items, equal versus point-proportional weighting, rounding, extra credit, letter boundaries and policy changes. Keep staff drafts separate from released learner results. These are proposed acceptance cases, not a new adopted grading policy.

Blackboard supports course group sets and assessment use, and documents effects of membership changes. That supports the need to design the complete transaction rather than only a grouping dropdown. [Create and Manage Groups](https://help.anthology.com/blackboard/instructor/en/interact-with-students/groups/create-and-manage-groups.html).

Proposed validation: create groups manually or randomly, find unassigned learners, assign one assessment, let a member submit for the group, show the same receipt to authorized members, then grade and release. Decide individual overrides, late join/withdrawal, membership snapshots, resubmission and TA assignment scope before treating it as complete. Keep grading groups distinct from staff navigation groups and course sections.

Calendar, communication and activity should share records

Blackboard documents personal events and a course-only calendar, including instructor-added office hours and schedules. Google documents personal notification settings and recurring-event edits. These are useful bounded references for the planner. Neither commits Whiteboard to Google Calendar feature parity. [Blackboard Calendar](https://help.anthology.com/blackboard/student/en/getting-started/calendar.html), [Google notifications](https://support.google.com/calendar/answer/37242), [Google recurring events](https://support.google.com/calendar/answer/37115).

Proposed validation: publish an exam and office-hour series; see them in course and combined views without duplicates; add a private work shift; edit one recurring occurrence; change the exam time and invalidate its old reminder. Private items must not become visible to professors/TAs. Test time zones and notification permission denial. Grading-task records should drive the TA calendar and work queue together.

Blackboard distinguishes announcement creation, scheduling and posting from its activity stream. Its instructor stream includes grading work. Whiteboard can extend S03/S11/S13 and role-aware S12 instead of introducing duplicate feeds. [Announcements](https://help.anthology.com/blackboard/instructor/en/interact-with-students/announcements.html), [Student Activity Page](https://help.anthology.com/blackboard/student/en/getting-started/activity-page.html), [Instructor Activity Page](https://help.anthology.com/blackboard/instructor/en/getting-started/activity-page.html).

Quiz integrity needs a separate decision

MDN documents visibility and focus signals; they describe browser state, not what a student did elsewhere. Its fullscreen guidance explicitly permits user/browser exit. Respondus describes a separate custom browser for application restrictions. This supports a distinction between ordinary web telemetry and a controlled exam environment; it does not prove any system eliminates cheating. [Page Visibility API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Page_Visibility_API), [Fullscreen guide](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Fullscreen_API/Guide), [Respondus LockDown Browser](https://web.respondus.com/he/lockdownbrowser/).

Recommendation, not an adopted policy: never label a focus-loss event “cheating” or automatically erase/cancel the whole attempt from a simple counter. Preserve saved work, disclose the chosen policy, distinguish connectivity/device interruptions, provide accessible recovery and staff review. Evaluate a secure-browser integration only if a partner requires it, with device, accessibility, support and cost implications. “Mouse tracking” is inaccurate terminology for tab/window visibility monitoring.

Tools, achievements and AI require clear scope

Software access depends on the institution, role and license. Google's school-account documentation distinguishes feature access by license; Cornell's service matrix is one institutional example of role-specific access. Whiteboard should show verified eligibility and access instructions, not promise Adobe/Gemini is universally free. [Google school accounts](https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/14620100?co=DASHER._Family%3DEducation&hl=en), [Cornell role-based services](https://it.cornell.edu/netids/it-services-available-your-role-cornell).

Blackboard's Achievements feature awards course badges against criteria. Proposed Whiteboard awards should be optional and separate from official grades unless an explicit grading rule says otherwise. Their existence elsewhere is not evidence that the first school needs them. [Achievements](https://help.anthology.com/blackboard/instructor/en/interact-with-students/achievements.html).

Blackboard's AVA illustrates a course assistant controlled by institution/instructor settings and scoped to student-visible content, with accuracy limitations. For Whiteboard, a later FAQ/navigation assistant could use published materials with citations and a staff escalation path. It must not reveal answer keys, held grades or other learners' data, bypass a course AI prohibition, or autonomously change grades. Provider, handling, evaluation and operating cost remain undecided. [AVA student documentation](https://help.anthology.com/blackboard/student/en/course-content-and-materials/ava-ai-virtual-assistant.html).

Proposed backlog order

These priorities are review judgments, not owner-approved implementation scope or delivery estimates.

  1. Core academic completeness: AR10 configurable grading policy; AR12 student course grades; AR13 groups and group assignments. Design them together so the learner outcome matches staff setup and release rules.
  2. Daily academic work: AR04 announcement authoring; AR06 course calendar; AR11 TA grading calendar; AR01 reminders; AR09 semester activity history. Follow with AR02 private planning and AR05 complete term/archive navigation.
  3. Academic access convenience: AR08 Tools directory and course-specific software access. Do not expand into institution administration to provide a useful directory.
  4. Optional/discovery work: AR14 achievements and AR15 assistant. AR07 assessment integrity needs feasibility/policy discovery before a feature decision; technical review should occur before promising restrictions.
  5. Preserve: AR03 no direct messaging, existing authority boundaries, immutable receipts and release snapshots, scoped TAs and truthful pending/offline states.

Candidate placement uses existing S02/S03/S05/S07-S13/S15-S17/S19/S21 and shared tools. Do not silently add destinations or change the 50-destination baseline: D61/D62 remain the recorded decisions. A design pass must explicitly review any route addition that becomes necessary. The wider campus work remains saved and outside the current focus.

Work performed and next checkpoint

Read both PDF pages and their screenshots; compared the 15 distinct topics with canonical map entries, academic renderer sources, the older showcase, decisions and state checklist; checked the primary documentation listed above. No product HTML, screen source, design tracker acceptance, route count or decision ID was changed. No tests, deployments, paid services or external messages were required for this documentation review.

Next checkpoint: review this classification and choose a bounded academic design backlog. Any later design or implementation should start from the complete workflows above, not from adding menu labels. This research does not start a backend/native build or reapprove the existing designs.
